The browser hits the Echo file route `GET /file/users/{username}/avatar` (the URL the API itself hands out — `convertUserFromStore` rewrites a base64 avatar into `/file/{user.Name}/avatar` at `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36`, where `Name` is `users/{username}`). ``` Route GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 FileServerService.serveUserAvatar — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 FileServerService.getUserByUsername — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 Store.GetUser — store/user.go:148 Store.ListUsers — store/user.go:135 Driver.ListUsers (store.Driver iface) — store/driver.go DB.ListUsers (sqlite) — store/db/sqlite/user.go:88 [MySQL: store/db/mysql/user.go:84 · Postgres: store/db/postgres/user.go:87] db.QueryContext — SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? — store/db/sqlite/user.go:152-172 ``` Per-hop notes: - **`serveUserAvatar`** (`fileserver.go:168`) first applies an access gate: when `s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()` is false, it requires a resolvable viewer via `s.getCurrentUser` and 401s otherwise (`fileserver.go:173-180`). It then takes `:identifier` from the path (`fileserver.go:183`). - **`getUserByUsername`** (`fileserver.go:715`) is a one-line adapter building `&store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}` — note the route param is treated as a *username*, not a UID. - **`Store.GetUser`** (`store/user.go:148`) consults `userCache` only when the find is by ID; a username lookup always falls through to `ListUsers` and takes `list[0]`, then populates the cache (`store/user.go:149-170`). - **`Store.ListUsers`** (`store/user.go:135`) delegates straight to `s.driver`, warming the cache for each row. - **Driver `ListUsers`** builds the `WHERE username = ?` predicate (`store/db/sqlite/user.go:127-129`) and scans `avatar_url` into `user.AvatarURL` (`store/db/sqlite/user.go:158`, `:189`). Back in the handler, the stored value is a data URI: `parseDataURI` (`fileserver.go:737`) regex-splits and base64-decodes it, the MIME type is checked against `avatarAllowedTypes` (`fileserver.go:75`, enforced at `:201`), security headers plus `Cache-Control` are set, and the bytes are written with `c.Blob` (`fileserver.go:207`). So the image never touches the filesystem or S3 — it lives inline in the `user.avatar_url` column. There is also a gRPC `UserService/GetUserAvatar` method (allow-listed for anonymous access at `server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go:25`), but the `` the web client renders points at the `/file/...` route above.
